bihar_raw_news.title: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster
bihar_raw_news.content: Tejashwi Yadav urges Centre to declare Bihar floods a national disaster RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to declare Bihar’s floods a national disaster and provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate assistance. He also sought enhanced rescue operations, farmer relief, an audit and a long-term flood resilience mission By IANS Published Date - 8 September 2026, 12:15 AM Patna: As severe floods continue to affect large parts of Bihar, Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging the Centre to declare the situation a national disaster and provide immediate financial assistance of Rs 5,000 crore to the state. More than a dozen districts have been affected by the floods, with lakhs of people facing difficulties caused by rising river levels, damaged infrastructure and disrupted connectivity. In his letter, Yadav said the situation had affected 20 districts and caused extensive damage to life, property and public infrastructure. He said flood-affected people were struggling to access basic necessities, including food, clean drinking water, medicines, electricity, cattle fodder and safe transportation. Yadav criticised the relief and rescue measures being undertaken by the Bihar government and the NDA-led Centre, describing the assistance as inadequate considering the scale of the crisis. He also accused the Bihar government and NDA leaders from the state of failing to secure adequate central assistance and a national-disaster declaration. The RJD leader argued that Bihar’s recurring floods are not solely a natural disaster but also reflect years of inadequate disaster preparedness, mitigation and adaptation. He pointed out that despite floods occurring almost every year, sufficient measures for a permanent solution have not been implemented. Yadav also raised questions over the state government’s financial preparedness for the crisis. He alleged that Bihar’s Contingency Fund and other financial resources had been diverted towards routine government expenditure, leaving insufficient funds for flood relief. The RJD leader called for an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s financial and disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation of the State Contingency Fund. In his letter, Yadav urged the Prime Minister and the Central Government to take immediate measures, including declare the devastating floods in Bihar a national disaster, provide Rs 5,000 crore in immediate financial assistance along with a special flood-relief package, deploy additional boats and other resources to flood-hit areas where road connectivity has been disrupted, deploy the Army and Air Force wherever necessary for rescue and relief operations and ensure assistance through helicopters, ensure adequate supplies of food, drinking water, medicines, animal fodder and temporary shelters, provide special financial assistance to farmers, labourers, livestock owners and affected families, and conduct an independent review or CAG audit of the state’s disaster-management preparedness and the utilisation and transactions of the State Contingency Fund. Yadav also called for a comprehensive, long-term Flood Resilience Mission to address Bihar’s recurring flood crisis. According to him, the mission should focus on river and embankment management, drainage systems, rejuvenation of water bodies, modern flood forecasting and improved water-management policies. national_raw_news.content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah today chaired the 28th meeting of the Western Zonal Council at Panaji in Goa. Addressing the gathering, Mr Shah said, there are no longer any disputes among the states of the Western Region, which is a major achievement. He emphasized that the Zonal Councils have evolved from forums for dispute resolution into platforms for monitoring the implementation of public welfare schemes. Mr Shah said that all the issues discussed in today’s meeting were related to monitoring. He noted that several disputes between States over rivers have also been resolved in the Zonal Council. Shah said the councils are also monitoring key welfare indicators, including child malnutrition, underweight and stunting, along with Aadhaar coverage and the implementation of Ayushman Bharat cards. Mr Shah said, over the last 12 years, Prime Minister Modi has strengthened cooperative federalism, with Zonal Council meetings increasing nearly threefold since 2014. He said, during 2004 to 2014, the total number of meetings of the Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees was only 25, whereas since 2014, a total of 71 meetings of the Zonal Councils and their Standing Committees have been held. He said 1,445 of a total of 1,893 issues discussed in these meetings have been resolved, reflecting the effectiveness of the councils and the spirit of Team India. Noting that the Western region is extremely important from several perspectives, the Home Minister said this region is the country’s largest economic, industrial and financial centre. He said, Goa contributes much more to economic growth than its geographical size would suggest due to advanced tourism, high per capita income and mines. He pointed out that since 2014, Prime Minister Modi has continuously worked, along with numerous administrative reforms, to transform the country’s economy into a rapidly moving economy. He said that Daman and Diu, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and the three states of the Western Zonal Council have also made a significant contribution towards achieving the growth rate of 7.8 per cent. Mr Shah said, the Western Region is known as the WEST Engine of the country’s economic growth. W stands for wealth and finance, which are generated in this region; E stands for exports and ports; S stands for start-ups and semiconductors; and T stands for tourism and the blue economy, in which the Western Region has the largest share in the country. The Home Minister said, recently, the country recorded a growth rate of 7.8 per cent in the first quarter of the financial year 2026-2027. Mr Shah further mentioned that the Indian economy recording such a growth rate amid global turbulence is a matter of pride . At the 28th meeting of the Western Zonal Council, several extremely important issues were discussed for the member states as well as for the country. These included the implementation of Fast Track Special Courts for speedy investigation and early disposal of cases of rape against women and children, issues related to the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112), issues related to food safety standards, Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, provision of brick-and-mortar banking facilities within the prescribed radius of every village, issues related to railway development projects, issues concerning environmental clearances, and others. In addition, issues of national importance were also discussed, including urban master planning, issues related to electricity supply, strengthening Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACSs), eliminating malnutrition among children through the Poshan Abhiyaan, reducing the school dropout rate among school children, participation of public hospitals in the Ayushman Bharat-Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana, and issues related to cybercrime and digital infrastructure, among others. The meeting was attended by Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and Administrator of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu Praful K Patel. Senior officials of the Central government and the state governments, as well as the Union Territory, also participated in the meeting of the council.

national_raw_news.title: 4 hours ago | National 148 Satya Niketan tragedy: Delhi HC directs MCD for highest level of inquiry to ascertain valid per...
national_raw_news.content: The Delhi High Court has directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to conduct an inquiry at the highest executive level into the collapse of a building at Satya Niketan in National Capital and examine whether the structure had been constructed and operated with valid permissions. Taking serious note of the incident, the court also directed the MCD to conduct a comprehensive audit of all paying guest (PG) accommodations and hostels under its jurisdiction within one week. The court directed that the inquiry into the collapsed building should specifically examine whether all requisite permissions had been obtained, identify officials responsible for any lapse or failure on the part of the authorities and specify the action proposed or taken against those found responsible. The directions came amid concerns over the safety of students residing in private PG accommodations and hostels, particularly in areas around Delhi University, where a large number of outstation students depend on such facilities due to limited hostel accommodation. As part of its directions, the court asked the MCD to inspect all PG accommodations falling under its jurisdiction within a week. The inspection will examine whether such premises are being operated in accordance with requisite permissions and applicable building bye-laws. The MCD has also been directed to ascertain the number of students residing in each PG accommodation. The court further sought details regarding the existence of a regulatory framework specifically governing PG accommodations and private hostels. It observed that responsibility cannot rest solely with building owners and that the concerned authorities also have a statutory duty to ensure compliance with safety and construction norms. The Delhi University has also been asked to provide details of the number of outstation students enrolled with it and the hostel facilities available to accommodate them. During the hearing, the court also raised concerns over alleged reckless and unauthorised construction by some PG operators. It also took note of assurances given by the MCD and Delhi Police that all possible steps were being taken and rescue operations were underway. The court expressed hope that the rescue efforts would be further intensified. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, who represented the Centre, the Delhi government, the Delhi Police and the MCD in the matter, assured the court that no stone would be left unturned in dealing with the incident. The High Court has directed the concerned authorities to place their responses and affidavits on record within ten days and listed the matter for further hearing on 25th of this month. The court was hearing a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in the matter relating to the building collapse. The directions come a day after a multi-storey PG building in Satya Niketan, a major student accommodation hub near Delhi University’s South Campus, collapsed, triggering a large-scale rescue operation and raising questions over construction and safety compliance.

national_raw_news.title: 6 hours ago | National 251 DAC clears acquisition proposals worth over Rs 1.10 lakh cr for Forces
national_raw_news.content: The Defence Acquisition Council (DAC) today cleared capital acquisition proposals worth over 1.10 lakh crore rupees for the defence forces. The approval was granted during a meeting of the Council held under the Chairmanship of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. The proposals include, procurement of Chemical Biological Radiological and Nuclear (CBRN) Recce Vehicles, High Mobility Vehicles (HMV), Self-Propelled Mechanical Mine Layers (MML), Advanced Light Helicopters (ALHs), Trawl Tanks and Sarvatra Bridge System for the Indian Army. For the Indian Navy, Acceptance of Necessity was accorded for the procurement of Arudhra Radars, Design and Development and subsequent procurement of Marine Gas Turbines (MGT). Arudhra Radar will replace the existing Air Route Surveillance Radars at various Naval Air Stations and MGT, a warship propulsion system, will reduce dependency on foreign vendors. Meanwhile, for the Indian Air Force, approval was granted to various proposals to enhance the war-fighting capability of fighters, transports and helicopters. Approval was also accorded for procuring Ground-Based Multi-Purpose Jammer (GBMPJ) and installing Defence Forces Secure Access Card (DEFSAC) System. Defence Ministry said that 98 percent of total procurements will be made from the Indian Industry. The CBRN Recce Vehicles will be capable of detecting, identifying, monitoring and marking of areas contaminated with CBRN agents. The HMVs will enhance operational capabilities, logistic support and mobility in challenging terrains. The MMLs will achieve the desired operational capability in terms of fast and responsive minelaying in difficult terrains. The ALHs will execute complex missions across all terrains and operational situations for the Indian Army and the Indian Air Force. The Trawl Tanks and Bridge System will be utilised to provide composite crossings to fighting formations during operations in varied terrains. The GBMPJ will provide effective jamming against radars of adversaries and DEFSAC will replace existing paper based Identity Card, Passes, Permits with an interoperable Radio Frequency Identification-based smart cards system.

national_raw_news.title: World Archery Para Series: Sheetal Devi confirms medal for India 7 hours ago 177
national_raw_news.content: Reigning world champion Sheetal Devi has confirmed a medal for India by storming into the women’s compound individual final on the third day of the stage three of World Archery Para Series in Ahmedabad today. In an all-Indian semifinal, the armless archer from Jammu defeated Sarita 145-143 to book her place in the gold medal clash. She will face Aizada Seidan of Kazakhstan in the final. Sarita will also have another opportunity to add to India’s medal tally when she will take on Wang Huiting of China in the bronze medal match. The women’s compound event thus gave India one confirmed medal and another still in the hunt, with world number one Sheetal eyeing the top podium finish. In the W1 women’s section, second-seeded Indian Swati Chaudhary set to fight for the bronze medal. Swati lost to sixth seed Liu Jing of China 1-7. In the compound Men’s section, reigning world champion and world number one Toman Kumar lost to top seed Ken Swagumilang of Indonesia 146-144 in the semifinal. He will fight for the bronze medal against Abbas Kahdim of Iraq. However, India’s campaign ended in the W1 men’s section after fifth seed Adil Mohamed Nazir Ansari and ninth seed Nurudin lost their respective quarterfinal matches. Athletes classified as W1 usually have an impairment in the top and bottom halves of their bodies, torso and at least three limbs and some W1 athletes have an assistant to help them load the bow.

national_raw_news.title: Commerce Minister urges pharma industry to utilise FTA opportunities for building India global destination for medicines 5 hours ago 106
national_raw_news.content: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal today called for India to build on its position as the pharmacy of the world and emerge as a global medical and healthcare destination. Addressing the inauguration of Pharma Mach Tech and Labnext Expo 2026 in New Delhi, Mr Goyal highlighted the growing importance of healthcare beyond treatment, encompassing prevention, wellness, caregiving, medical devices, telemedicine, teleconsultation, innovation and research and development for newer drugs and modern equipment. The Minister also urged the industry to utilise the opportunities arising from India’s free trade agreements. Mr Goyal called upon stakeholders to participate in the country’s development journey and work towards ensuring access to quality education, healthcare and opportunities for all. He said that the medical and pharmaceutical machinery, consumables and related sectors represent a growing field with significant potential to create crores of jobs, thousands of business opportunities and lakhs of new startups, particularly in the medtech field. The Minister also called for strengthening the startup incubation ecosystem for medtech, medical equipment and consumables, along with improvements in design, copyrights, patent laws and the intellectual property ecosystem. Emphasising the need for self-reliance in research, medicines and medical equipment, Mr Goyal called for technology partnerships, stronger buyer-seller relationships and joint ventures to advance self-reliance in the sector. The Minister said India should aim not only to provide high-quality healthcare to every Indian but also to provide wellness and healthcare services to the world from India.

national_raw_news.title: Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK - Kashmir Convener
national_raw_news.content: Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK - Kashmir Convener J&K Media Delegation from Kerala begins Seven-Day Press Tour to JK By Desk Editor Published on Sep 7, 2026 Share Convener News Desk Srinagar, September 7: A 13-member media delegation from Kerala has embarked on a seven-day press tour to Jammu and Kashmir from September 6 to 12, 2026. The tour is being organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Kochi, with the objective of providing journalists from Kerala an opportunity to gain first-hand insights into the developmental initiatives, infrastructure projects and achievements in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. On the first day of the tour, the delegation visited the Press Information Bureau office in Srinagar. Shri Qazi Salman, Director, PIB Srinagar, welcomed the members of the delegation and provided an overview of the media and communication landscape in Kashmir. He also interacted with the visiting journalists and shared insights into the functioning of PIB in the region. Later in the day, the delegation visited Gulmarg, the picturesque hill station located in Baramulla district of Jammu and Kashmir, and experienced the region’s rich natural landscape and scenic beauty. During the week long tour, the media delegation will visit various developmental projects and important locations across the Union Territory. The press tour aims to familiarise the participating journalists with the developmental transformation taking place in Jammu and Kashmir and provide them an opportunity to interact with the stakeholders. The press tour is part of PIB’s efforts to facilitate wider awareness and informed reporting on significant developmental initiatives being undertaken across different regions of the country. national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Finance Union Finance Minister meets delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) Scheme of Performance Linked Incentives (PLI) to Executives of Public Sector Banks kept in abeyance in response to Employees’ concerns Posted On: 07 SEP 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi The Union Finance Minister today met with a delegation of bank employees representing different Public Sector Banks (PSBs) led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh. The delegation raised various issues relating to the banking sector including review of ex-gratia, medical facility for retired employees, revisiting the present structure of Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme applicable for the employees of PSBs, and other concerns related to employees. The concerns expressed by bank employees were taken cognizance of, and in response to the representation received on the PLI structure, it was decided to keep in abeyance the implementation of the PLI Scheme dated 19.11.2024 for FY 2025–26 and take up the same during the ongoing Bipartite Settlement/ Joint Note discussions.
